newsitem.title: UK: Unilever drops on ice cream row report.
newsitem.headline: Unilever drops on ice cream row report.

text.p: Shares in Unilever Plc dropped on Monday after a report in the Financial Times said Mars had resumed its attack on the ice cream sales practices of the Anglo-Dutch consumer products giant.
The stock was down 10-1/2p at 13.58-1/2 stg by 0826 GMT.

The FT said Mars had attacked Unilever's sales practices in the Irish republic, saying it had persisted with behaviour found by the European Union to be anti-competitive and involving the supply of freezers to shopkeepers for stocking its brands.

The report said the EU was concerned too few retailers had bought their own freezers despite a previous agreement with Unilever to increase sales, though Unilever responded by saying a document from Mars contained "misinformation and innuendo."

John Campbell, an analyst at Paribas Capital Markets, said the report raised some potentially major issues but a final resolution of the issue was some way away and it was hard to see Unilever losing all along the line.

"The story relates to Ireland which in the overall context is relatively small, but if a principle is established it could be difficult for the EU to take a contrary position in other countries so the stakes are high," said Campbell.
Unilever spokesman Mike Haines dismissed the Mars claims. "Our business is not designed to reduce consumer choice, and it does not do so. It is fair competition."

The European Commission is expected to produce a fresh "statement of objections" to Unilever's current sales practices within the next two weeks, which will then be subject to discussion with the company.
